strengths: Valuable dataset contribution: SpatialSceneQA with 61k high-quality synchronized RGB-D, FOA audio, and fine-grained 3D annotations is novel and will benefit the community

Clear problem motivation and strong empirical evidence: Demonstrates that 2D AV-LLMs completely fail on joint reasoning tasks (~44% accuracy) while JAEGER achieves 99.2%, effectively motivating 3D spatial modeling
Well-executed experimental methodology: Comprehensive ablation studies, appropriate metrics, cross-evaluation demonstrating generalization, and clear baseline comparisons across three categories
Technically sound approach: Principled integration of depth-aware positional encoding, dual-path audio processing, and learnable Neural IV with clear architectural design
Strong performance on joint audio-visual reasoning: Near-perfect accuracy on reasoning tasks demonstrates the value of explicit 3D modeling for spatial disambiguation
Clear presentation and good documentation: Well-written with effective figures, detailed implementation details, and comprehensive coordinate system definitions facilitating reproducibility
weaknesses: Entirely simulation-based evaluation without real-world validation: All results on SoundSpaces 2.0 synthetic data; no evidence of generalization to real acoustic environments, depth sensor noise, or actual sound-emitting objects. This is critical for a spatial reasoning task and significantly limits impact

Limited technical novelty of individual components: Depth-aware positional encoding (existing in N3D-VLM, Video-3D LLM), FOA representation (standard), LoRA fine-tuning (standard practice). Neural IV improvement is incremental—essentially replacing STFT with CNN. Single-source DoA improvement minimal (2.21° vs 2.16°)

Incomplete baseline comparisons: BAT trained for only 5 epochs (potentially under-tuned); SAVVY (most relevant prior work) mentioned but not compared; visual baselines only tested zero-shot; no computational cost comparisons; no comparison of inference latency

Artificial reasoning task setup: Visual objects are synthetic (Hunyuan3D-generated), perfectly aligned with audio sources, from limited speaker pool (120 instances). Generalization to real speaker designs and placements unclear

Limited acoustic realism in dataset: Only 1-4m source-receiver distance within single rooms; LibriSpeech read speech (not real-world variability); no dynamic sources; geodesic distance constraints limit complex acoustic paths; no background noise or real-world interference

Insufficient analysis of Neural IV: No visualization of learned patterns; architecture choices (7-layer CNN with specific kernels/strides) not justified; cross-evaluation shows degradation persists (16.36° on overlap when trained on single source); computational overhead not reported

Missing critical technical details: FOA sample rate not specified; audio clip duration unstated; LLM parameter count absent; components fine-tuned vs. frozen unclear; memory requirements and training time not reported; no failure case analysis

Modest improvements on core perception tasks: Audio DoA comparable to BAT (2.21° vs 2.16°); overlapping DoA still 13.13° error; 3D IoU of 0.32 is modest; depth encoding ablation shows only 0.03 IoU improvement, suggesting RGB features already encode geometry

Questionable generalization claims: Synthetic speakers, perfect depth, ideal microphone array, clean speech. No evidence of robustness to depth noise, FOA channel imbalances, visibility changes, or out-of-distribution speaker types

Limited path to real-world deployment: Paper doesn't discuss how real embodied agents would access perfect depth/FOA, or address sim-to-real gap for acoustic properties; no discussion of failure modes or practical constraints

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine gap in current AV-LLMs' inability to perform 3D spatial reasoning
Comprehensive SpatialSceneQA dataset with 61k samples, diverse tasks, dense 3D annotations, and clear construction pipeline
Thorough experimental evaluation with appropriate metrics, multiple baseline categories, ablation studies, and cross-evaluation analysis
Technically sound methods with reasonable architecture design and proper ablations validating design choices
Strong performance on synthetic reasoning tasks (99.2% accuracy) and competitive perception results
weaknesses: Critical limitation: entire evaluation is simulation-only with zero real-world validation or sim-to-real experiments, severely limiting practical impact and generalization claims given known sim-to-real gaps in perception

Incremental technical novelty: 3D-aware visual encoding uses established techniques (depth projection, sinusoidal encodings); Neural IV is straightforward CNN replacement of STFT with modest improvements (2.21° vs 2.95°), lacking theoretical justification

Problematic baselines: no direct baseline with identical modality, unfair comparison to Qwen2.5-Omni which lacks multi-channel audio input, missing comparisons to traditional signal processing methods

Questionable generalization: small scene database (130 training scenes), limited audio diversity (only LibriSpeech read speech), synthetic speaker models (120 similar floor-standing speakers), no cross-dataset evaluation or real acoustic scenario testing

Shallow Neural IV analysis: no explanation of why CNN outperforms STFT, no comparison to alternative learned representations or domain-specific architectures, limited testing across diverse acoustic scenarios

Suspiciously high reasoning performance (99.2%) raises overfitting concerns; no error analysis, failure case visualization, or evidence that learned spatial reasoning is robust beyond synthetic distribution
Missing critical details: task loss weighting strategy unspecified, computational costs not reported, no sensitivity analysis for LoRA hyperparameters, missing ablations on component interactions
Limited reasoning scope: Tasks D-E are simple classification identifying which visible speaker matches audio; no open-ended spatial reasoning or unobserved object reasoning

Insufficient analysis of what model learns: no investigation of how depth vs. spatial audio contribute, no visualization of learned features or failure modes, no analysis of performance degradation with distance/elevation/noise

strengths: Addresses a well-motivated gap in current AV-LLMs by explicitly modeling 3D spatial relationships through RGB-D and multi-channel FOA, with clear technical justification
Introduces SpatialSceneQA, the first large-scale dataset with degree-level azimuth/elevation supervision paired with RGB-D and FOA, valuable for the community
Demonstrates strong empirical results on joint audio-visual reasoning (99.2% accuracy vs. 44.0% for 2D baseline), convincingly showing the necessity of 3D modeling
Thorough experimental validation including comprehensive ablations (Tables 3-5), cross-scenario evaluation, and component-wise analysis that effectively isolate contributions
Neural IV shows meaningful improvements in overlapping-source localization (13.13° vs. 16.09° classical IV) and better generalization across scenarios
Clear presentation with well-organized sections, informative figures, and detailed task definitions
Compelling ablation demonstrating catastrophic performance drop (43.8% accuracy) when removing FOA encoder, empirically validating the 3D architecture necessity
weaknesses: Critical limitation: All evaluation is on synthetically generated data from SpatialSceneQA with no real-world validation or sim-to-real transfer analysis, limiting evidence of practical applicability
Modest improvements in individual perception tasks (single-source DoA 2.21° vs. BAT 2.16°, overlap DoA still 13.13°, 3D IoU of 0.32 is moderate) that don't match strong joint reasoning results

Limited architectural novelty—combines existing techniques (Qwen2.5-Omni, depth encoding from Wang et al. 2025, LoRA, intensity vectors from Tang et al. 2024) with incremental Neural IV contribution (STFT→CNN is natural evolution)
Unfair baseline comparisons: BAT trained for only 5 epochs (under-tuned), N3D-VLM and Qwen3-VL-8B tested only zero-shot without fine-tuning
Practical applicability concerns: FOA audio is uncommon in real-world scenarios; high computational requirements (8-24 GPUs) limit reproducibility

Dataset limitations: Only 130 HM3D scenes for training, all audio from clean LibriSpeech recordings (no natural speech/noise/music), 120 synthetic speakers may lack diversity, visibility constraint (500 pixels) may bias toward closer speakers, no inter-annotator agreement reported

Insufficient robustness analysis: No evaluation of sensitivity to depth noise (common in real RGB-D sensors), no analysis of error distributions or systematic failure modes, missing evaluation on >3 simultaneous speakers

Technical design choices lack justification: CNN architecture for Neural IV (kernel/stride sizes), choice of sinusoidal positional encoding for depth, element-wise product in intensity computation; no exploration of alternative learnable representations
Depth sensitivity not evaluated—real sensors have noise/artifacts that could significantly impact performance
Ethical considerations inadequately addressed—brief impact statement overlooks privacy/surveillance implications of audio-visual tracking systems

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing real gap in current AV-LLMs: identifies the dimensionality mismatch between 2D perception and 3D environments clearly

Neural Intensity Vector demonstrates meaningful improvement: Table 3 shows superior generalization to mismatched training/test scenarios (14.85° vs 19.25° for overlapping sources), and Table 5 shows it outperforms Classical IV, particularly in challenging settings

Comprehensive experimental evaluation with thorough ablations: matched-input architectural ablation (Table 7) isolates gains from framework design; cross-evaluation (Table 3) validates generalization; component analysis (Table 5) justifies each module
Valuable dataset contribution: SpatialSceneQA is the first large-scale spatial audio-visual benchmark with degree-level supervision, 61k samples, and proper train/val/test partitioning across scenes
Strong reproducibility: detailed implementation details (LoRA hyperparameters, learning rates, GPU counts), promise to release code/models/datasets, and clear dataset construction pipeline
Solid technical soundness: dual-path audio architecture (semantic/spatial disentanglement) is principled; 3D-aware positional encoding through depth projection is well-executed
weaknesses: Severely limited real-world validation undermines practical applicability claims: Appendix A's STARSS23 evaluation restricted to 753 clips with single-speaker, stationary sources; azimuth error reaches 76.7° (vs 2.21° in simulation)—massive sim-to-real gap suggests learned features may not transfer to real acoustic environments

Limited algorithmic novelty: depth-aware positional encoding is established (Zheng et al. 2025, Wang et al. 2025); Classical Intensity Vectors are standard; Neural IV is primarily CNN replacing STFT—an incremental contribution; main novelty is integration and dataset rather than fundamental innovation

Impractical hardware modality choice: FOA requires 4-channel microphone arrays uncommon in consumer/robotics; Appendix C shows FOA significantly outperforms binaural (99.2% vs 85.0%), but this narrow advantage comes at cost of deployment practicality; most real-world systems use stereo or monaural audio

Evaluation demonstrates ceiling effects on controlled benchmark: near-perfect reasoning accuracy (99.5%, 99.2%) with 2-3 candidates, but Table 9 shows accuracy drops to 72.5% with 6 candidates when trained on only 160 samples; suggests results are sensitive to controlled conditions and may not generalize to realistic unconstrained scenarios

No downstream task evaluation: paper lacks demonstration on actual embodied AI tasks (robot navigation, object retrieval, audio-visual event detection); unclear if framework improves performance on real-world applications beyond the constructed benchmark

Entirely synthetic audio and objects limit generalization: SoundSpaces 2.0 acoustic rendering may not capture real reverberation complexity, microphone noise, or speaker variability; 120 procedurally-generated loudspeaker models don't reflect acoustic diversity of real-world speakers

Weak baseline comparisons: BAT trained for only 5 epochs (not fully optimized); Qwen2.5-Omni incapable of audio DoA; no comparisons with recent 3D-grounding LLMs adapted to this setup; no comparison of FOA vs binaural under equal training budgets

Missing critical analysis: no error case discussion or failure mode analysis; no investigation of what 3D geometry teaches vs. spatial audio alone beyond broad component ablation; no computational cost analysis; limited analysis of generalization to out-of-distribution acoustic conditions
